newsitem.title: GERMANY: E.Europe coffee firms should stress quality - Tchibo.
newsitem.headline: E.Europe coffee firms should stress quality - Tchibo.

text.p: Eastern European coffee markets may contribute to global demand growth but only if consumers are convinced that coffee is a quality beverage, Hasso Kaempfe, board member at Tchibo-Frisch-Roest-Kaffee GmbH.
"...there is no reason why coffee consumption...should not increase along with the growing prosperity (in the region)," Kaempfe told the F.O. Licht World Coffee Conference.
"Yet if the average coffee quality gets worse and worse, consumers will tend to switch to soft drinks and other hot beverages...."
Kaempfe said low-quality coffees in unattractive packaging were on offer from companies in the region, which discredited the image of coffee as a luxury item.
Cheap robusta blends and coffees from old stocks were noticeable in the mass markets in Hungary and the Czech republic.
The use of coffee filters was not spreading easily, with many consumers prefering to brew Turkish-style coffees.
After five years of western presence in the region, markets in Hungary and the Czech republic were now dominated by large western European companies.
It was unlikely that new suppliers would be able to establish themselves in these two countries.
In Poland and Slovakia, local suppliers held large market shares but they needed to make structural changes over the next five years to keep up with international competition.
Russia and the Baltic and Balkan states were also attractive markets in the long term, but their volumes to date were still negligible.
Tchibo, which had been active in the region since the early 1990s, was disappointed with volume sales, price wars and low profit margins.
